To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

novel diiron complexes with a Fe2(mu- OMe)2 core have been studied as models of active sites of nonheme-iron-containing enzymes and that two types of ligands, parallel and twisted, have been found to exist.

the novel bis(mu-metoxo)diirons with phenoxyl ligands have a unique Fe2(mu-OME)2 core structure and show the existence of two or more distinct high-valence redox states resonating with the radical(s) of the phenolate ligands.
novel diiron complexes with the Fe2(mu-OCH3)2 core were prepared and structurally and electrochemically characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and electrochemical studies on novel bis(mu-metoxo)di iron complexes as models of the nonheme iron containing enzymes.

the development of a new class of diiron(III) complexes with a bis(mu-methoxide) bridging ligand, which is a novel structural motif in the diiron chemistry, and with the study of their electronic structures by electrochemical and spectroscopic methods.
the development of novel diiron complexes with a Fe2(mu-OR)2 core and the study of their redox properties as models of nonheme diiron enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bis(mu-alkoxo)di-iron(III) complexes with a twisted ligand folding are more likely to form a Fe(IV) center in the active site of the nonheme iron(IV)-containing enzymes.
the present complexes are good models for the diiron center of the enzymes.

the Fe(III) and Fe(II) ions of the Fe(III)(mu-OMe)Fe(III) core in these complexes are electronically isolated from the phenolato ligands, and that the Fe(II)Fe(II) and Fe(III) Fe(III) complexes have a relatively high reactivity toward O-2 and H-2O2, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Fe2(mu-O)2 core can accommodate two phenolato ligands with different orientations, and the phenolate groups are electronically coupled with the Fe2(muO)2 core, leading to a variety of electronic configurations of the Fe(IV) and phenoxyl radicals.
the bis(mu-OMe)-bridged diiron complexes have two types of folding, and that the phenolate groups are electronically coupled with each other through the core.
the Fe2(mu-X)2 core (X = O, NR, and MeO) is an excellent platform for stabilizing high-valent iron species and phenoxyl radical, which are key intermediates in the catalytic cycle of nonheme enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fe(III) Fe(IV) state of the diiron core is a viable intermediate for oxygen activation in nonheme iron-oxo enzymes.
the Fe2(mu-O)2 core can be a platform to stabilize the Fe(III) and Fe(III,IV) states in addition to the Fe(II) and Fe(II,III) states.
we have found a novel type of Fe2O2 complex, which is a good model for the active site of the nonheme diiron enzymes.
